recognize_zh: 中央中性球核分成約7葉以上（hypersegmented neutrophil），右側另一顆中性球也有多葉；背景紅血球偏大並有橢圓形巨紅血球（macro-ovalocytes）與不規則形紅血球，符合惡性貧血（pernicious anemia）等巨母細胞性貧血。
features: Central neutrophil with about seven or more discrete nuclear lobes (hypersegmentation)
Second neutrophil at right edge also shows multiple lobes
Mature clumped chromatin with thin interlobar strands; normal pale granular cytoplasm
Red cells are large with oval macrocytes (macro-ovalocytes) and mild poikilocytosis, including a crenated cell and irregular forms
Neutrophil diameter slightly larger than usual relative to RBCs
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a neutrophil with marked nuclear hypersegmentation, containing approximately seven or more lobes connected by thin chromatin strands, and a second multilobated neutrophil at the edge of the field. The red cells are predominantly macrocytic with oval macrocytes and mild poikilocytosis. Hypersegmented neutrophils (six or more lobes, or more than 5% with five lobes) together with macro-ovalocytes indicate impaired DNA synthesis. Findings are consistent with megaloblastic anemia, as seen in pernicious anemia due to vitamin B12 deficiency.

ddx.vs: Folate deficiency produces identical smear findings; separation requires serum B12, folate, methylmalonic acid and homocysteine levels.
Morphology is indistinguishable, and medication history with normal vitamin levels identifies drug effect.
MDS shows dysplastic neutrophils that are more often hypogranular and hyposegmented (pseudo-Pelger) with normal B12/folate, rather than classic hypersegmentation.

ddx.dx: Hereditary neutrophil hypersegmentation / renal failure or iron deficiency
ddx.vs: These cause only mild hypersegmentation without macro-ovalocytes or megaloblastic marrow change.
